title: Analysis of the CueR Constitutive Activator Variant (CueRCA) through Crystallography and DNA-Binding
abstract: The sensing and regulating of metal ions is crucial for the survival of bacterial organisms such as Escherichia coli. Due to its high toxicity, copper is regulated through a homeostatic copper efflux system. In this system, the CueR protein acts as a transcriptional regulator of two copper efflux genes by distorting DNA upon copper-binding. My project strived to characterize the role of an individual protein domain, the C-terminal helix, in the metal-bound activator conformation of CueR, as it undergoes the induced change for transcriptional activation. To determine this role, a mutant variant of the CueR protein was created that exhibits clear Cu(I)-independent transcription activation (CueRCA) at all copper concentrations. The constitutive activator variant was overexpressed and purified for characterization by Native gel shift assay and crystallography. Crystallization conditions were screened and optimized to produce CueRCA crystals that diffracted to ~2.45 Å. I found that (1) CueRCA does bind to DNAs of different lengths, and (2) all CueR residues are present in the CueRCA structure, except the metal-binding loop (MBL). This supports my hypothesis that the CTH ultimately stabilizes the activator confirmation and that CueRCA superactivation does not result from changes to other residues. The structure of CueRCA has therefore provided evidence of both key details of transcription activation in E. coli and a similar mechanism shared with other metalloregulators and ligand-binding proteins in both eukaryotes and prokaryotes. This indicates an approach that has been evolutionarily conserved and remains adaptable to the binding of different ligands with protein/DNA complexes.
